Total. How many altogether? The total is five.

Between. Six is between five and seven.
Next. One, two, three. What comes next? Four!
Order. One, two, three, four, five. The numbers are in order.
A number track. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
Point. Point to each number as you say it.
Missing. Six, blank, eight. Seven is the missing number.
Compare. Look at two sets. Which set has more?
More. Five is more than four.
Fewer. There are fewer snails than spiders.
Less. Seven is less than nine.
Same. Three apples and three apples. They are the same.
Equal. Four and four are equal.
A pair. Two things that go together. A pair of boots.
Even. Four is an even number. Two pairs, none left over.
Odd. Three is an odd number. One pair and one left over.
Pattern. Odd, even, odd, even. It is a pattern.
Elephant. An elephant is living. Animals move around and eat other things.
Tree. A tree is living. Plants make their own food.
Cactus. A cactus is a plant. It lives in dry places.
Teddy bear. A teddy bear is non-living. A toy is not alive.
Car. A car moves, but it is non-living.
Chopsticks. Chopsticks are made of wood. Wood used to be alive, in a tree.
Plant. Plants are living things. Most plants are green.
Flower. The flower is the part where the seeds are made.
Leaf. The leaf makes food for the plant.
Stem. The stem holds the leaves and flowers up.
items.sentence: The stem holds the leaves up.

items.say: Roots. The roots collect water. The roots hold the plant still. A carrot is a root!
Seeds. Some plants have flowers which make seeds. A nut is a seed.
Tomato. A tomato plant has leaves, a stem, roots and flowers.
Magnifying glass. Use a magnifying glass to observe a plant.
items.sentence: I look with a magnifying glass.

items.say: Light. Plants use light to make food. Plants need light.
Water. Plants need water. Water moves, but it is not alive.
Grow. When plants get bigger, we say they grow.
items.find: Which one is a young plant?

items.say: Box. Marcus covers one plant with a box. No light!
Cave. Plants can't grow in a cave because there is no light.
items.sentence: Plants can't grow in a cave.

items.say: A dry plant. If plants do not have enough water, they can die.
Garden. In a garden we can learn about plants.
items.sentence: I love to play in the garden.

items.say: Gardener. The gardener gives the plants lots of light and water.
Bee. A bee is a living thing. Bees visit flowers.
Alive. Plants and animals are alive.
Living. Plants and animals are living things.
Non-living. A teddy bear is non-living. It is not alive.
Animal. Animals move around and eat other things.
Group. Put things into two groups: living and non-living.
Look. Use your eyes to look at the picture.
Observe. Look carefully. Observe the plant parts.
Name. Name the parts of a plant: leaf, stem, flower, root.
Parts. All plants have parts that we can see.
Similar. These two apples are similar. They are nearly the same.
Different. An apple and a banana are different.
Model. Make a model of a plant.
Question. Marcus asks a question: why is this plant bent?
Answer. Here is the answer: it is growing towards the light.
Investigation. Do a science investigation to find the answer.
Predict. Say what you think will happen.
Explain. Explain why plants need water.
Record. Record your results. Write or draw them.
Table. Record your results in a table.
Mix blue and yellow. You get green!
Mix red and yellow. You get orange!
Mix red and blue. You get purple!
Paper clip. We can measure with paper clips.
Same. Red and red are the same.
Different. Red and blue are different.
What's your favourite colour? My favourite colour is red.
Do maths. I do maths at school.
